properties.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 7 at 11:41AM PST until November 8 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves 22 to 24
feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides
will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt
Bay. Up to one half foot of saltwater inundation above ground
level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between
8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is
predicted.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 AM to 10 PM PST
Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 10 AM to noon PST
Sunday. High tide is at 10:21 AM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit
tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours
before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay
including parks and roads with only isolated closures expected.
Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in the Arcata
Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Dangerous surf
conditions and localized beach erosion. Beachcombing is highly
discouraged!

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The large surf on Sunday will coincide with
high astronomical tides and high tidal anomalies. This will
allow significant runup onto area beaches and may impact
normally dry land or even roads or parking lots.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 7 at 11:34AM CST until November 9 at 9:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
Multiple rounds of locally heavy rainfall are expected between
Saturday night and early Monday morning across the Rio Grande Plains
and Brush Country.  The first round is most likely between midnight
and mid-morning Sunday, when 1 to 2 inches with locally 3 or more
inches of rain may fall. The second round is expected Sunday night
into early Monday morning, when an additional 1 to 3 inches with
locally 4 inches or more may fall.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Deep South Texas, including the following
counties, Brooks, Jim Hogg and Zapata.

* WHEN...From 6 PM CST this evening through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of arroyos and
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Some
arroyos may rise out of their banks near where heaviest rains fall.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Storm drains
and ditches may become clogged with debris. Highest concern
includes locations in Zapata, such as Medina Addition, as well as
more populated areas of Hebbronville and Falfurrias, including
along state highways 16, 359, and 285.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Potential for heavy rainfall, including two windows where
rainfall rates could reach 2 inches per hour for two hours both
late tonight and early Sunday morning, and again Sunday night
through mid morning Monday.
- Concern is highest across populated areas, including the cities
of Zapata, Hebbronville, and Falfurrias.  Flood prone areas along
or near arroyos in Jim Hogg and Zapata are at most risk, but high
water could also flood open rangeland.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 10 PM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous breaking waves can knock people off their
feet and sweep them into the ocean. Driftwood and debris in
powerful surf can injure or even kill people on the beach
observing the ocean. High surf will result in erosion to
beaches, dunes, and bluffs and may cause damage to roads,
trails, and coastal structures.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Seas 22 to 26 feet.
properties.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water and well back from the
surf zone. This includes staying off jetties, piers, and other
coastal structures. Never turn your back on the ocean and keep
children and pets close. Know the tides and forecast conditions.
Follow warning signs and respect barriers.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 6 at 8:17PM CST until November 9 at 12:00PM CST by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of south Texas, including the following areas,
Aransas Islands, Bee, Coastal Aransas, Coastal Kleberg, Coastal
Nueces, Coastal Refugio, Coastal San Patricio, Duval, Goliad,
Inland Kleberg, Inland Nueces, Inland Refugio, Inland San Patricio,
Jim Wells, Kleberg Islands, La Salle, Live Oak, McMullen, Nueces
Islands and Webb.

* WHEN...From Saturday afternoon through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Widespread forecast rainfall amounts of 2-4 inches will be common
across South Texas with high end amounts approaching 5 inches.
Isolated amounts exceeding 5 inches remains a possibility,
especially in the vicinity of training and slow moving storms.
While soils will be able to absorb most of this moisture, the
higher rainfall rates can quickly lead to localized, urban
flooding and in locations with poor drainage.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.
